_doc: Canonical WGS84 geographic registry for the atlas, built by docs/changes/map-timeline/trace/kml_geo_registry.py from the KML inventory. Coordinates are the KML's OWN lon/lat and are never projected here: the separate MapLibre geographic mode wants geographic coordinates, and round-tripping them through a 26.96px-RMS artwork fit would lose precision for nothing. Anything that needs artwork pixels projects at the point of use, through the shipped atlas-georef.json. Ids are stable across re-imports of the same source. TWO PROPERTIES THAT LOOK LIKE FAULTS AND ARE NOT. (1) The registry is not confined to North America: the pre-war divisions folder holds England, Scotland, Bavaria and Shaanxi among others, so only 49.1% of pre-war-state vertices project onto the artwork's land, and that is the source being worldwide rather than the import being wrong. (2) One feature genuinely crosses the antimeridian, the Aleutian arm of Northwest Commonwealth, spanning lon -177.38 to +178.18; a consumer that treats longitude as a simple interval will draw it right around the globe.

properties.name: Capital Wasteland
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: The Capital Wasteland is the general name given to the ruins of Washington, D.C. and the region surrounding it. It stretches from Raven Rock in the northwest to Rivet City in the southeast, with what's left of the Potomac River dividing it roughly in two.

properties.name: Mojave Wasteland
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: The Mojave Wasteland is the region synonymous with the Mojave Desert, spanning portions of the pre-War states of California, Nevada, and Arizona.

properties.name: The Commonwealth
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: The Commonwealth, also called the Commonwealth Wasteland, is the name given to the area around Boston - it derived from the pre-war Commonwealth of Massachusetts, itself part of the greater New England Commonwealth. A large part of it is taken up by the Glowing Sea, a heavily irradiated region created by a nuclear detonation during the Great War.

properties.name: New California / Core Region
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note:
New California, also known as the Core Region, is a loosely-defined area geographically centered around the former US state of California. For much of its existence, it has been dominated by the New California Republic.

** Depicted territory is speculated, though Vault City, Lost Hills, and the Boneyard are all said to be part of it. **

properties.name: Baja
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: Baja is a region south of New California, consisting of the Baja California Peninsula that was once part of Mexico. The New California Republic has a presence within it.

properties.name: The Boneyard (formerly Greater Los Angeles)
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: The Boneyard, also known as Angel's Boneyard after it became part of one of the states of the New California Republic, is the overall title given to the collective of settlements built in remains of Greater Los Angeles. It is named for its devastated skyscrapers reduced to their metal "skeletons" and for the literal skeletons of the dead that littered the city after the Great War.

properties.name: Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion area
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads

properties.name: The Glowing Sea
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: The Glowing Sea is the name given to a large, extremely irradiated region in the Commonwealth. It was created during the Great War when a high-yield atomic bomb hit a nuclear reactor.

properties.name: The Divide
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: The Divide is a violent land torn apart by quakes and skin-flaying wind storms to the northwest of the Mojave Wasteland. It was created in the 23rd century when numerous old nuclear warheads in their silos simultaneously detonated.

properties.name: Zion Canyon
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: Zion Canyon was spared from most of the horrors of the Great War, and remains an unspoiled wilderness. It is the traditional home of the Sorrows tribe. Recently, missionaries from New Canaan in the north have arrived in the region, attempting to convert the locals to Mormonism. That in itself would not have been a threat to the peace, but the White Legs, a hostile group with whom the Mormon Church

properties.name: Mount Desert Island / The Island
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note:
Mount Desert Island, also known as simply the Island, is a large island of the coast of Maine.

Before the Great War, it was a famous holiday location. After the war, there were small settlements all over the island, however a radioactive fog drove the locals away.

properties.name: Oasis
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.note: Oasis is a region in the Capital Wasteland full of trees and plants due to the FEV mutated tree-human Harold, who is rooted in the ground and cannot move. A small community of 'Treeminders' worship him.

properties.name: The Forest
properties.sourceFolder: Regions, travel routes, and significant pre-war roads
properties.geometryCaveat: The KML held several polygons here; the inventory flattened them to one coordinate list, so the parts cannot be separated without re-parsing the KML. Treated as a single ring.
